Each line has an Inkora TJ-5 inkjet printer that prints lot and expiry on cartons, and a camera that inspects every carton. A line integration service, PackBridge (supplied by Corvane Systems), takes product data from the site ERP and pre-fills each print job. Several changes were made at the site between late September and October 2026.","presentingRequest":"The client's quality lead asks for an independent view. Kestrel Distribution's goods-in system rejected three lots of Veltranol 20 mg tablets, 28s (VT-2641, VT-2644, VT-2652), because the printed expiry was later than the maximum shelf life in Kestrel's product file. Cartons and 2D codes read EXP 10/2029. The approved batch records, generated from the ERP batch master, state EXP 10/2028 (24 months from bulk manufacture). All three lots were packed on Line 3, night shift, 9-23 Oct. Veltranol is the only product Kestrel buys from the site. Immediate action: the three lots are on hold and Kestrel is quarantining the stock it received. Status of other Veltranol lots: not yet reviewed."},{"id":"E2","stage":"S1","source":"Email from Gareth Lindqvist, Site Director, to the client quality lead, 13 Nov 2026","sourceType":"leadership-account","text":"'I want to be straight with you. All three lots came off Line 3 nights, which is where our new agency cohort started on 30 September. Setup on these lines lets the operator overwrite the pre-filled expiry, and our night supervisor tells me the new starters weren't always confident with that screen. I'm satisfied this is a people issue. This week I'm removing the agency operators from labelling duties and issuing formal warnings, and we'll retrain everyone. I don't expect you'll see this again.'"},{"id":"E3","stage":"S1","source":"Site change-control log summary, 15 Sep - 31 Oct 2026","sourceType":"change-record","text":"CC-301 (28 Sep): Inkora TJ-5 printer firmware 4.2 to 4.3 on all four line printers, to fix intermittent dropping of the final lot-code character. CC-309 (1-24 Oct): Regulatory Affairs material-master update, 12 edits across 9 products, arising from the annual product review and approved variations. CC-311 (1 Oct): camera font re-teach, Line 3. No changes to PackBridge (line integration service) were recorded in the period."},{"id":"E4","stage":"S1","source":"Interview notes, Dana Whitcombe, night-shift supervisor, 13 Nov 2026","sourceType":"manager-account","text":"'At job setup PackBridge fills in the lot number and expiry. The printers log every job's setup values if QA want them.'"},{"id":"E5","stage":"S1","source":"Email from Corvane Systems support (PackBridge vendor) to site QA, 14 Nov 2026","sourceType":"vendor-account","text":"'PackBridge reads product master data from your ERP when a job is created and works out expiry as manufacture date plus shelf life. 3 Oct at 16:42, Regulatory Affairs entered an approved future shelf life of 36 months for both Veltranol SKUs under CC-309. Jobs before 4 Oct were all correct, so the fault did not exist earlier. Two other products got future-dated shelf-life values on 20 Oct. C2 shows the 24-month value had been in place since 2023."},{"itemId":"I-H5","expected":"unknown","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C2"],"allowedEvidence":["C2","C1","E1","C7"],"tags":["scope","live-unestablished"],"rationale":"C2 shows HX-15-30 and MR-05-14 received future-dated shelf-life values on 20 Oct, so the same fault could affect them. The claim is live but unestablished."},{"itemId":"I-R1","expected":"contradicted","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C1"],"allowedEvidence":["C1","C3","C4","C9","E2","E4"],"tags":["leadership-narrative","confounded"],"rationale":"The evidence counts against the link itself. There is a mechanism: PackBridge reads SHELF_LIFE_M at job creation (E5, C8), and the payload field changes from 24 to 36. The covariation is clean, with 24 before the edit and 36 after it. The main rivals (operator override, firmware) are ruled out by C1, and no PackBridge change was recorded (E3). PackBridge ignoring the valid-from date is a co-cause, but it does not weaken the link."},{"itemId":"I-A1","expected":"harmful","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C1"],"allowedEvidence":["C1","E2","C3","C9"],"tags":["punish-wrong-party","leadership-narrative"],"rationale":"Operators did not cause the errors. It is not among the best actions."},{"itemId":"I-A4","expected":"premature","weight":2,"requiredEvidence":["C2"],"allowedEvidence":["C2","C1"],"tags":["premature","scope"],"rationale":"This would be right if H5 were confirmed. The open question of why PackBridge ignored the valid-from date does not block A2, because the reset plus the independent QA check works whatever the answer is."}],"discriminatingReads":["C1","C2"],"lowValueReads":["C12","C13","C14"],"optimalReadPath":["C1","C2"],"authoringNotes":"Sequential design: the initial file steers away from master data. Batch-record headers generated from the ERP are correct (E1), the vendor says PackBridge cannot send future values (E5), CC-309 looks routine, and the leadership and supervisor accounts point to operators. The natural first read is the printer job records (C1), which E4 says exist. C1 moves the fault upstream (payload already wrong, no overrides) and shows the payload shelf-life basis switching from 24 to 36 between 3 and 4 Oct. That date falls inside the CC-309 master-data window in E3, which identifies C2 as the discriminating second read rather than the tempting PackBridge configuration (C8). C8 shows USE_VALID_FROM = Y, so reading it leaves R3 at association-only and A2 at premature. Non-redundancy: only C1 settles H1, H2, H4, R1, R2 and A1 (no other item records overrides or payload versus print). Only C2 settles R3 (causal) and A2 (preferred), because no other item shows the VT edit, its time or its valid-from date. C11 deliberately omits edit values. C10 omits work-order printouts. C4 omits the product schedule, so H5 stays unknown across the whole catalogue. C2 read alone, together with E5 and C8, leaves operator override live. Reading in the order C2 then C1 also reaches the key, but nothing in the initial file makes C2 the obvious first pick. Traps: night-shift confound, firmware date-library note, QA manager's long-standing theory, vendor and impact-assessment assurances, signs of hesitant operators."}}

case.title: Expiry dates a year too late on Veltranol cartons at Ashcombe Packaging, Wrexley
case.setting: Ashcombe Packaging Services' Wrexley site is a contract packager running four blister-and-carton lines (Lines 1-4). Each line has an Inkora TJ-5 inkjet printer that prints lot and expiry on cartons, and a camera that inspects every carton. A line integration service, PackBridge (supplied by Corvane Systems), takes product data from the site ERP and pre-fills each print job. Several changes were made at the site between late September and October 2026.
case.presentingRequest: The client's quality lead asks for an independent view. What caused the wrong expiry dates on Veltranol cartons? Is the site director's plan right? What should the site do now? You may collect at most two further items of evidence.

initialEvidence.source: Deviation DV-26-114 opening record, QA, 12 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: Deviation DV-26-114, opened 12 Nov 2026 (QA). Kestrel Distribution's goods-in system rejected three lots of Veltranol 20 mg tablets, 28s (VT-2641, VT-2644, VT-2652), because the printed expiry was later than the maximum shelf life in Kestrel's product file. Cartons and 2D codes read EXP 10/2029. The approved batch records, generated from the ERP batch master, state EXP 10/2028 (24 months from bulk manufacture). All three lots were packed on Line 3, night shift, 9-23 Oct. Veltranol is the only product Kestrel buys from the site. Immediate action: the three lots are on hold and Kestrel is quarantining the stock it received. Status of other Veltranol lots: not yet reviewed.

initialEvidence.source: Email from Gareth Lindqvist, Site Director, to the client quality lead, 13 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'I want to be straight with you. All three lots came off Line 3 nights, which is where our new agency cohort started on 30 September. Setup on these lines lets the operator overwrite the pre-filled expiry, and our night supervisor tells me the new starters weren't always confident with that screen. I'm satisfied this is a people issue. This week I'm removing the agency operators from labelling duties and issuing formal warnings, and we'll retrain everyone. I don't expect you'll see this again.'

initialEvidence.source: Site change-control log summary, 15 Sep - 31 Oct 2026
initialEvidence.text: CC-301 (28 Sep): Inkora TJ-5 printer firmware 4.2 to 4.3 on all four line printers, to fix intermittent dropping of the final lot-code character. CC-305 (30 Sep): six agency operators added to the night shift on Lines 3 and 4. CC-309 (1-24 Oct): Regulatory Affairs material-master update, 12 edits across 9 products, arising from the annual product review and approved variations. CC-311 (1 Oct): camera font re-teach, Line 3. No changes to PackBridge (line integration service) were recorded in the period.

initialEvidence.source: Interview notes, Dana Whitcombe, night-shift supervisor, 13 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'At job setup PackBridge fills in the lot number and expiry. The operator checks the printer screen against the work-order printout, which also comes out of PackBridge, then presses Confirm or overrides with a reason code. Operators can't touch PackBridge or the ERP, only the printer screen. Some of the agency lads were slow on that screen in their first fortnight. I had to talk two of them through it. The camera reads every carton and kicks out anything smudged or cut short, about three in a thousand. It checks the print matches the job. It doesn't know the batch record. The printers log every job's setup values if QA want them.'

initialEvidence.source: Email from Corvane Systems support (PackBridge vendor) to site QA, 14 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'PackBridge reads product master data from your ERP when a job is created and works out expiry as manufacture date plus shelf life. Master-data records carry a valid-from date, and PackBridge only ever uses the value in effect on the job date. It cannot send a future value to the line. No other site has reported date errors on this version. We suggest you look at manual overrides at the printer.'

initialEvidence.source: QA manager note to file, 14 Nov 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'I wouldn't assume this started in October. Kestrel only switched on its shelf-life check at goods-in on 1 October, so before that nobody outside would have caught a late expiry. Our in-process checks compare the carton to the work order, so they wouldn't have caught it either. I'd treat everything since the last audit as suspect until shown otherwise.'

catalogue.title: Inkora printer job records, Veltranol 20 mg, all lines, 1 Jun - 10 Nov 2026
catalogue.source: Inkora TJ-5 job database export, pulled by Engineering, 15 Nov 2026
catalogue.text:
Export of 47 Veltranol jobs (28s and 56s) on Lines 1-4. Each job record has: date and shift, line, operator ID, expiry received in the PackBridge payload, shelf-life basis in the payload (SHELF_LIFE_M), operator override (Y/N), expiry printed, camera result.
- 2 Jun to 3 Oct (30 jobs): SHELF_LIFE_M = 24, and expiry matches the batch record. This includes 4 jobs after the 28 Sep firmware change, 3 of them on Line 3 nights, 30 Sep to 3 Oct, set up by agency operators.
- 4 Oct 22:10 to 10 Nov (17 jobs): SHELF_LIFE_M = 36, and expiry is 12 months later than the batch record. 15 of these jobs ran on Line 3 nights. 2 ran on Line 1 day shift (21 Oct, 29 Oct; operators D-102 and D-114, permanent staff). Those 2 lots are in the finished-goods warehouse.
- All 47 jobs: override = N, printed string identical to payload string, camera result PASS (matched to job data).

catalogue.title: ERP material-master change history, shelf-life fields, 1 Sep - 10 Nov 2026
catalogue.source: ERP audit-trail report run by IT, 15 Nov 2026
catalogue.text:
Audit trail for field SHELF_LIFE_M. Each value is stored with a valid-from date.
- VT-20-28 and VT-20-56 (Veltranol): new value 36 entered 3 Oct 16:42 by user RA-OKONJO under CC-309, valid-from 01 Mar 2027, with the note 'per approved variation - lots manufactured from 01-03-2027 only'. The existing value of 24 (valid since 2023) was kept and is still the value in effect today.
- The other 10 CC-309 edits cover 7 products. Eight of them have a valid-from date equal to the entry date. Two have later dates, both entered 20 Oct with valid-from 01 Jan 2027: HX-15-30 (36 to 24) and MR-05-14 (24 to 30).
- No other changes to SHELF_LIFE_M in the period.
This report does not include packing history for the products listed.

catalogue.title: Agency operator induction and competency records, night shift, Sep - Oct 2026
catalogue.text: Six agency operators (A-201 to A-206) finished induction 26-29 Sep. Four were signed off as competent in labelling setup (SOP PK-044) on 2 Oct and two on 9 Oct. The night supervisor countersigned the two later sign-offs after those operators had already run three jobs each. Assessment notes include 'hesitant at override screen' (A-203) and 'needs reminder to check work-order printout' (A-205). No assessment records an override error.

catalogue.title: Shift rosters and line assignments, 1 Sep - 10 Nov 2026
catalogue.text: The rosters list names, shift and line only. The product schedule is held in the planning system and is not included. From 30 Sep, each Line 3 night shift had two agency operators and one permanent operator, and each Line 4 night shift had the same mix. Day shifts on all lines had only permanent operators. D. Whitcombe was night supervisor throughout. Night-shift overtime rose from 6% of hours in September to 11% in October.

catalogue.title: Inkora TJ-5 firmware 4.3 release notes and CC-301 validation summary
catalogue.source: Inkora release notes; site engineering validation file
catalogue.text: Release notes, 4.3: 'Fix: final character of variable text fields could be dropped at high line speed. Change: date/time formatting library updated for improved locale support. Known issues: none.' CC-301 validation summary (site engineering, 27 Sep): test prints of lot and expiry fields on each printer, 20 cartons per line, all matched the input. Truncation test passed at 220 cartons/min. The engineers typed the test inputs by hand. They were not received from PackBridge.

catalogue.title: Camera reject statistics, Lines 1 and 3, 1 Sep - 10 Nov 2026
catalogue.text: Line 3 reject rate: 0.31% (Sep), 0.29% (Oct), 0.33% (Nov to date). Line 1: 0.27%, 0.30%, 0.28%. Reject reasons: smudge or low contrast 61%, missing or truncated character 33%, no read 6%. After the CC-311 font re-teach (1 Oct), Line 3 no-read rejects fell from 0.04% to 0.01%. Across both lines, 412 cartons with truncated lot or expiry codes were rejected in the period.

catalogue.title: Kestrel Distribution complaint correspondence, 11 - 14 Nov 2026
catalogue.text: Kestrel's goods-in check has been live since 1 Oct. It compares the scanned expiry with the maximum shelf life held for each SKU. It flagged three Veltranol lots, and Kestrel quarantined 1,140 packs. Kestrel received four other Veltranol lots from the site in October that its system did not flag, because they were booked in by hand during a scanner outage on 17-18 Oct. Kestrel asks whether those lots are also affected and wants a written explanation by 28 Nov.

catalogue.title: PackBridge interface configuration export, Lines 1-4
catalogue.source: PackBridge admin console export by IT, 15 Nov 2026
catalogue.text: Mapping: EXPIRY = MFG_DATE + SHELF_LIFE_M, end-of-month format MM/YYYY. SHELF_LIFE_M source: ERP material master, read when the job is created. Parameter USE_VALID_FROM = Y. Software version 7.2.1, installed 14 Mar 2025. Last configuration change: 14 Mar 2025 (CC-188, initial go-live). Interface error log: no errors for 1 Sep - 10 Nov.

catalogue.title: Interview notes, four agency operators, 14 Nov 2026
catalogue.text: All four say they never overrode an expiry on Veltranol and 'just checked it matched the work order and pressed Confirm'. A-203: 'The first week I didn't really know what the override button did, so I never touched it.' A-205: 'We were told the system does the dates.' None of the four were told why they were being interviewed, and two asked whether they would lose their placement.

catalogue.title: Batch packaging records, lots VT-2641, VT-2644, VT-2652
catalogue.text: In each record, the header shows the approved expiry 10/2028, taken from the ERP batch master. Line clearance is signed. Operators signed in-process checks hourly and a QA technician every four hours, each reading 'carton print checked against work order - conforms'. Under SOP PK-044, work-order printouts are thrown away at the end of each job and are not in the records. QA release reviews on 27 Oct, 30 Oct and 4 Nov say 'record complete'. No carton specimen is kept with the record.

catalogue.title: CC-309 change-control form and impact assessment
catalogue.text: Raised by Regulatory Affairs on 22 Sep. Scope: 12 material-master edits across 9 products, arising from the annual product review and approved variations. The edit list is held in the ERP. Impact assessment, section 4, 'Downstream systems': 'Master-data values only. PackBridge applies valid-from dates; no impact on packaging line systems. No line testing required.' Approved by QA and Engineering on 30 Sep. Closed 25 Oct.

catalogue.title: Line 3 shift handover log, October 2026
catalogue.text: October entries mention: printhead cleans (5 Oct, 19 Oct), carton magazine jam (11 Oct), camera re-teach checked OK (2 Oct), agency operator A-205 sent home sick (16 Oct), and 'Veltranol run long, bulk arrived late' (22 Oct). No entry mentions expiry dates, overrides or label queries. Several night entries are initialled but not dated.

catalogue.title: Line 3 packing-room temperature and humidity records, 1 Sep - 10 Nov 2026
catalogue.text: Logged every 15 minutes. Temperature 19.2-22.8 C (limits 15-25 C). Relative humidity 38-54% (limits 30-60%). No excursions. There were two sensor dropouts (7 Oct 03:10-03:40; 26 Oct 01:00-01:15), and those gaps were filled from the room's second probe. No operator complaints about ink drying were recorded.

catalogue.title: Brightwell Staffing contract and Q3 2026 supplier review
catalogue.text: The contract runs Apr 2026 - Mar 2027 for up to ten packaging operators. The agency handles basic GMP induction, and the site handles SOP training and competency. Q3 review: fill rate 94%, two late starts, rated 'meets expectations'. No quality incidents were attributed to agency staff before October. The renewal discussion is set for January 2027.

catalogue.title: Internal data-integrity audit report, June 2025
catalogue.text: Observation 3 (minor): 'Master-data changes are assessed for regulatory impact but not routinely for effect on downstream line systems.' CAPA-25-071 was assigned to IT, due Mar 2026. Status: open, extension requested. Observation 5: printer audit trails are enabled, protected from editing and reviewed quarterly, rated satisfactory. Observation 7: training records were sometimes signed after the activity, rated minor.

hypotheses.text: Operators entered or overrode the wrong expiry dates during line setup.
The printer firmware upgrade changed the expiry dates as they were printed.
The wrong expiry dates were already in the data sent to the printers, before any operator action.
Wrong expiry dates on Veltranol cartons began before the late-September changes and went undetected.
Products other than Veltranol have also been packed with wrong expiry dates.

actions.text: Remove the agency operators from labelling duties and issue them formal warnings, as the site director proposes.

Reset the Veltranol shelf-life records in the ERP so that only the value approved for current lots can be read. Extend the hold to every Veltranol lot packed since those records last changed. Require a second-person QA check of printed expiry against the approved batch record at each setup until the cause is fully resolved. Inspect retained cartons of any other product whose shelf-life record changed in October.
Commission a site-wide reconciliation of printed expiry against batch records for every lot packed in the past 12 months.
Begin over-labelling held and warehouse stock of other products with corrected expiry dates, on the assumption that they carry the same fault.
Switch off the camera's expiry-field verification on Lines 1 and 3, since it passed every faulty carton and gives false assurance.

truth.groundTruthNarrative: On 3 Oct at 16:42, Regulatory Affairs entered an approved future shelf life of 36 months for both Veltranol SKUs under CC-309. The entry was valid only for lots manufactured from 1 Mar 2027. The ERP kept 24 months as the value in effect, so batch-record headers stayed correct. PackBridge reads SHELF_LIFE_M when a job is created, and it took up the 36-month value from the next job onward (4 Oct 22:10). It did this despite the vendor's claim and the USE_VALID_FROM setting. Every Veltranol job from then until 10 Nov was sent an expiry 12 months too late. Operators made no overrides. The printers printed exactly what they received, and the camera passed the cartons because they matched the job data. The link to the night shift is a scheduling coincidence. Agency operators ran correct jobs from 30 Sep to 3 Oct, and permanent day-shift staff on Line 1 produced two faulty lots. The firmware change on 28 Sep came before six days of correct prints. Jobs before 4 Oct were all correct, so the fault did not exist earlier. Two other products got future-dated shelf-life values on 20 Oct. Whether they have been packed since, and so misprinted, is not established. The site director's plan targets the wrong people. The right response is to remove the future value from the read path, extend the hold, add an independent expiry check against the batch record, and inspect the other products.

answers.rationale: C1 records override = N and a printed string identical to the PackBridge payload on all 47 jobs. Agency operators ran correct jobs from 30 Sep to 3 Oct, and permanent day-shift staff produced two faulty lots. C15 confirms the printer audit trail is protected and reliable. The operators' hesitancy (C3, C9, E4) is real but did not result in any edit.

The firmware went in on 28 Sep, and four jobs after that printed correctly. The errors start only on 4 Oct, and in every job the printed string equals the payload string, so the printer did not alter dates. The 'date/time library updated' note in C5 is a red herring that C1 rules out.

C1 shows the PackBridge payload already carried SHELF_LIFE_M = 36 and the late expiry before any operator action, with no override. C2 shows where the 36 came from. This refutes the vendor's claim in E5.

The QA manager's suspicion (E6) is plausible from the initial file. But C1 shows all 30 Veltranol jobs from 2 Jun to 3 Oct used a 24-month basis and matched the batch records. C2 shows the 24-month value had been in place since 2023.

C2 shows HX-15-30 and MR-05-14 received future-dated shelf-life values on 20 Oct, so the same fault could affect them. However, C2 says packing history is not included, and nothing else shows whether those products were packed since. Kestrel buys only Veltranol (E1), so the lack of complaints about other products tells us nothing. The claim is live but unestablished.

The evidence counts against the link itself. No overrides occurred, agency-run jobs before 4 Oct were correct, and permanent day staff produced the same error. The night-shift pattern comes from scheduling, not from who staffed the line.
The upgraded printers printed correct dates for six days, and in every job the printed output equals the received payload. So the firmware did not produce the wrong dates.

The order of events fits: the edit was entered 3 Oct 16:42 and the first faulty job ran 4 Oct 22:10. There is a mechanism: PackBridge reads SHELF_LIFE_M at job creation (E5, C8), and the payload field changes from 24 to 36. The covariation is clean, with 24 before the edit and 36 after it. The main rivals (operator override, firmware) are ruled out by C1, and no PackBridge change was recorded (E3). PackBridge ignoring the valid-from date is a co-cause, but it does not weaken the link.
Operators did not cause the errors. Warnings punish the wrong party, signal to the client a false explanation, and leave the real fault in place. No live rival hypothesis involves operators.

Only C2 shows that the Veltranol ERP record holds a not-yet-effective 36-month value that PackBridge is reading. That makes the reset correct, and 3 Oct is the date from which the hold should run. The second-person check against the batch record is an independent check that the camera and the work-order check lack. Inspecting other products addresses H5 without assuming its outcome. Without C2 the reset would be premature.

Reasonable diligence that does no damage. But C1 and C2 bound the fault to jobs created after the October edits, so a 12-month site-wide review is slower and less targeted than A2. It is not among the best actions.

This would be right if H5 were confirmed. But it is not yet established that other products were packed with wrong dates, and inspecting retained cartons would settle that quickly. Over-labelling with correct dates would cause no lasting damage if H5 proves false.

The camera passed the faulty cartons only because they matched the job data. It still rejects smudged and truncated codes, about three in a thousand (E4), including 412 truncated codes (C6). Switching it off removes a working protection, whichever hypothesis is true.

C1 and C2 together establish the source, the start date and the scope for Veltranol, which is enough to commit to A2. The open question of why PackBridge ignored the valid-from date does not block A2, because the reset plus the independent QA check works whatever the answer is.

truth.authoringNotes: Sequential design: the initial file steers away from master data. Batch-record headers generated from the ERP are correct (E1), the vendor says PackBridge cannot send future values (E5), CC-309 looks routine, and the leadership and supervisor accounts point to operators. The natural first read is the printer job records (C1), which E4 says exist. C1 moves the fault upstream (payload already wrong, no overrides) and shows the payload shelf-life basis switching from 24 to 36 between 3 and 4 Oct. That date falls inside the CC-309 master-data window in E3, which identifies C2 as the discriminating second read rather than the tempting PackBridge configuration (C8). C8 shows USE_VALID_FROM = Y, so reading it leaves R3 at association-only and A2 at premature. Non-redundancy: only C1 settles H1, H2, H4, R1, R2 and A1 (no other item records overrides or payload versus print). Only C2 settles R3 (causal) and A2 (preferred), because no other item shows the VT edit, its time or its valid-from date. C11 deliberately omits edit values. C10 omits work-order printouts. C4 omits the product schedule, so H5 stays unknown across the whole catalogue. C2 read alone, together with E5 and C8, leaves operator override live. Reading in the order C2 then C1 also reaches the key, but nothing in the initial file makes C2 the obvious first pick. Traps: night-shift confound, firmware date-library note, QA manager's long-standing theory, vendor and impact-assessment assurances, signs of hesitant operators.
